gap: No result ChatGPT got states that PCWorld's Christopher Null tested two of these skimmers the same way and got opposite results on running without a plug: the WYBOT F1 never ran a full day before its battery died, even in Texas summer sun, while the Aiper EcoSurfer S2 ran 24 hours nonstop and used only about 25% of its battery.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited pages. The Hook Up's test (thesmarthomehookup.com, 2026-08-21) did not include the WYBOT F1. Its Betta was the Betta Neo, not the SE or SE Plus. It has leaf counts out of 20, Aiper's overnight drain of 3.46% per hour, and hours of full sun needed: about 5.7 for the Aiper and about 6.6 for the Beatbot. The Hook Up's recommendation page gives no measurements. Robotdoorstep (2026-11-06) says it did not test hands-on and lists only maker specs for the F1: a 33 W panel, a 7 L basket and no stated runtime. I also checked results ChatGPT got but did not cite. Bob Vila tested the F1 but gave no numbers. Digital Trends' Aiper review says the battery fell about 20-25% overnight, so the Aiper half is partly covered there. Poolrobotlab says it does not test products. No result has a measured battery result for the F1, and none puts the F1 and the Aiper side by side from one tester using one method.
decides: It shows the WYBOT F1 should not be offered as a skimmer that runs without plugging in. It is the cheapest skimmer on our page at $299.98, and our page currently says only 'Not stated by WYBOT' for its runtime. The finding also backs the Aiper EcoSurfer S2 as the pick for running on sun alone. Two named testers now agree on that: PCWorld (24 h nonstop for about 25% of the battery, and it kept a 10-hour daily schedule through weeks of rain) and The Hook Up (3.46% per hour, about 5.7 h of sun). The Beatbot iSkim stays a strong option. Digital Trends never had to charge it during a month-long test, but measured leaf pickup for it disagrees between testers.

findings.label: Full day on solar alone (PCWorld)
findings.value: Never managed a full day before the battery died, even in Texas summer sun
findings.source_title: Wybot F1 Pool Skimmer review: A noisy but effective pool cleaner (PCWorld, Christopher Null, 2025-06-18)
findings.note: Quote: 'I was never able to get the robot to run for a full day without its battery dying, even under the summer sun of Texas.' Also: 'Even on relatively sunny days, I often found the robot didn't run at all during the day in standard mode because it had never fully recharged.' The F1 has a 33 W panel feeding a 5,200 mAh battery.

findings.label: App battery reading vs. actual (PCWorld)
findings.value: App showed 98%; true level after restarting the app was 13%
findings.source_title: Wybot F1 Pool Skimmer review: A noisy but effective pool cleaner (PCWorld, Christopher Null, 2025-06-18)
findings.note: The battery reading in the app did not update until the app was force-quit and restarted.

findings.label: Leaf capture (PCWorld)
findings.value: About 85% of test leaves after about 4 h of running
findings.source_title: Wybot F1 Pool Skimmer review: A noisy but effective pool cleaner (PCWorld, Christopher Null, 2025-06-18)
findings.note: The leaves the robot missed sank to the floor. The F1 has a 7 L basket. The reviewer called it the most effective leaf skimmer he had used, but very loud.

findings.label: 24 h nonstop run, including overnight (PCWorld)
findings.source_title: Aiper EcoSurfer S2 review: Mostly hands-off pool cleaning that works (PCWorld, Christopher Null, 2026-05-04)
findings.note: Quote: 'I also ran it nonstop for 24 hours, including overnight, and it only lost about 25 percent of battery.' It has a 5,200 mAh battery (the same capacity as the F1's) and a 24 W panel. Aiper rates it at 30+ h.

findings.label: Daily schedule through bad weather (PCWorld)
findings.value: Never stopped on a 10-hour-a-day schedule through weeks of rain and overcast weather
findings.source_title: Aiper EcoSurfer S2 review: Mostly hands-off pool cleaning that works (PCWorld, Christopher Null, 2026-05-04)
findings.note: The reviewer concluded that 'most users will almost never have to resort to manually charging the EcoSurfer once it's in the water.'

findings.label: Leaf capture (PCWorld)
findings.value: About 80% of synthetic leaves; the surface was clear after about 3.5 h
findings.source_title: Aiper EcoSurfer S2 review: Mostly hands-off pool cleaning that works (PCWorld, Christopher Null, 2026-05-04)
findings.note: The robot started fully charged. The rest of the leaves sank, and a couple stuck to the tile at the waterline. This is the same reviewer and roughly the same method as the F1 test (about 85% over about 4 h).

findings.label: Overnight drain and sun needed (The Hook Up)
findings.value: 3.46% battery per hour with no sun; about 5.7 h of full sun to run nonstop
findings.source_title: Solar Pool Skimmers – Beatbot, Aiper, & Betta vs. Generic – The Hook Up (2026-08-21)
findings.note: From a cited rival, included for comparison. Method: an overnight run with no solar input, logging battery % against runtime. The Hook Up rated the Aiper the most efficient of the seven skimmers it tested.

findings.label: Overnight use and solar recharge (Digital Trends)
findings.value: About 20-25% of battery used overnight; recharged from 10% to 100% in under 2 h of sun
findings.source_title: Aiper Surfer S2 Review: the pool skimmer champion (Digital Trends, Ian Bell, 2025-08-25)
findings.note: Three weeks of testing. This review was in ChatGPT's results but not cited.

findings.label: Charging during a month-long test (Digital Trends)
findings.value: Never needed charging in about one month
findings.source_title: Beatbot Sora 30 and iSkim review (Digital Trends, Ian Bell, 2026-09-28)
findings.note: Quote: 'I never needed to charge it for the month I had it during this review period.' It cleared the surface in about an hour, which the reviewer says is half the time the Aiper Surfer took. Beatbot rates it at 28 h with no sun, from a 10,000 mAh battery and a 24 W panel.

findings.label: Sun needed and leaf pickup (The Hook Up)
findings.value: About 6.6 h of full sun to run nonstop; 18 of 20 leaves in a 1-hour test
findings.source_title: Solar Pool Skimmers – Beatbot, Aiper, & Betta vs. Generic – The Hook Up (2026-08-21)
findings.note: From a cited rival. In the same test, the Aiper took 15 of 20 leaves and the Betta Neo took all 20.

findings.label: Leaf capture with the pool pump off (The Gadgeteer)
findings.source_title: Beatbot Sora 70 and iSkim review (The Gadgeteer, Vincent Nguyen, 2026-06-26, updated 2026-11-02)
findings.note: This conflicts with The Hook Up's 18 of 20 (90%). The methods differ: The Gadgeteer ran with the pump off, while The Hook Up used a 1-hour run with 20 leaves.

findings.label: Durability (Bob Vila)
findings.value: Rear propellers stopped working after about 12 months of use; covered by warranty
findings.source_title: The Best Robotic Pool Skimmers of 2026, Tested by Pool Owners (Bob Vila, Paul Rankin, 2026-07-24)
findings.note: Owner-tester in Florida, running on solar. This is the only measured or timed figure for the Betta SE I found from a named tester.
